$comment: AUTHORITATIVE documentation registry (ADR-W-041, docs/06w-decisions-workspace.md; issue #904).
server/__tests__/docs-hygiene.test.ts READS this file. Do not restate these enumerations in prose
or hardcode them in a test — an enumeration living in a test is how docs/06c and src-analytic/
CLAUDE.md became invisible to the ADR-resolution guard while it reported green.
Adding a doc, a product, an ADR log or an orientation file means editing THIS file.
The two grandfather lists (index.grandfathered, frIds.grandfathered) are asserted EXACT, not
'at most': a new omission fails the suite rather than joining a growing list of exceptions.
They shrink to empty as #904 Phases 2-3 land, and each names the issue that will empty it.
Files that load into EVERY session and must stay orientation, not chronology (ADR-W-002, #452).
Ceilings sit ABOVE current size on purpose: a guard that fires on a legitimate addition gets
relaxed, and then there is no guard. src-analytic/CLAUDE.md was missing here until #904 -- the
fourth product's orientation file was unguarded from the day the tree was created.
WHY these numbers are what they are, which failure each guard catches, and why token budget is
the wrong axis to argue them on: ADR-W-042 in docs/06w-decisions-workspace.md. Read it before
changing a ceiling -- the doctrine is deliberately NOT restated here, because a JSON comment is
not a discoverable or linkable home for reasoning.
$raiseLog is the data series that ADR keeps referring to: every raise appends date, file, new
value, size at the time and why, so the growth curve stays visible and the next raise is argued
from data rather than memory.

$raiseLog.why: ADR-W-002 / #452. Set at the post-cleanup size + ~15%, after the file was cut from 188 KB (90% duplicated ADR chronology). A round number, not a derived one.

#904 Step 3. Measured: +2,607 B over 28 days (~93 B/day), and ALL of it structural -- products 3 and 4, the shell/ tree, standing rule 5, the fix-round machinery. Zero chronology. The 44 B left was a wall, not a cadence. 24000 restores roughly six weeks between forced prunes; the growth drivers (adding two products) are largely spent, so the real rate should fall. Operator ruling.

$comment: path -> { idPrefix, contractFrom }. idPrefix builds the id-matching regex, so a log listed here
is automatically VISIBLE to the resolution guard -- docs/06c-decisions-analytic.md was absent
from the old hardcoded list, making every ADR-AG-* id unresolvable-by-omission rather than
checked. Headings are matched as '^#+' because the logs mix '## ADR-N' and '### ADR-N' (390 vs
120 in 06-decisions.md alone); a '^## ' matcher silently skips a quarter of them.
contractFrom = the first id required to carry the ADR-W-041 **Requirements:** / **Design:**
lines. Each is set to (current max + 1) so all 815 existing ADRs are grandfathered by id and no
allowlist is needed -- EXCEPT 06w, deliberately set to 41 rather than 42 so ADR-W-041, the ADR
that mandates the lines, is the first one bound by its own rule.
Keyed by products.json id, plus 'workspace' and 'server' which ship no builder but do own
contracts (the shell/ chrome, the admin dashboard, the proxy). The guard cross-checks that every
products.json id appears here, so builder N+1 cannot arrive without its docs being accounted for.
A null path is a DECLARED gap and must carry 'pending' with the issue that closes it -- that is
the difference between a known debt and an oversight.

$comment: docs/README.md must reference every docs/*.md. The grandfathered list is the exact set of
omissions on 2026-09-05 and is emptied by #904 Phase 2 (Step 4).
Every FR-* cited anywhere in docs/ must be DEFINED in a registered requirements doc. A definition
is the bold declaration form '**FR-XX-N (Tier)**'; everything else is a citation. The matcher
excludes a preceding letter so 'NFR-SE-1' is not read as a definition of 'FR-SE-1' -- that false
positive appeared twice during the audit that produced #904.
FR-RV-7 is a REAL dangling reference found by this guard on the day it was written: cited by
FR-RV-4 and FR-RV-6, defined nowhere. Grandfathered rather than fixed in-flight, per #904's
'gaps are filed, not fixed' rule; resolved by Phase 2 (Step 5, the 02 truth pass).
The proportional gate of ADR-W-041: a doc-only change runs these instead of the ~10-minute full
suite. Measured 2026-09-05: 9 files, 655 tests, 2.1s.
This gate is the ONLY protection a doc change gets. ci.yml carries 'paths-ignore: docs/**', so a
docs-only push runs no CI lane at all -- a doc edit that breaks a test surfaces on someone's next
CODE push, attributed to the wrong commit. That is why the list is derived rather than recalled.
'derived' is CHECKED, not trusted: the guard rescans every test file for a quoted docs/*.md path
and fails if any match sits outside this gate, so a new doc-reading test joins by itself. This is
the ADR-394 discipline (a hand-kept exclusion list is how the fast tier stopped meaning anything)
applied to the doc gate. The scan is what caught the three readers a hand-written grep missed --
including two BYTE-MATCH gates, src/theorems (docs/07) and src-complex/formulas (docs/29), where
editing the doc alone turns the suite red.
'registryGuards' read the JSON registries (BOUNDARIES/products/DOCS) rather than docs/*.md, so no
scan derives them; sibling-safety also matches the scan because it uses docs/ paths as classifier
FIXTURES. The asserted invariant is therefore 'every scan match is somewhere in the gate', not a
clean partition between the two lists.
#905. ci.yml's `paths-ignore` is WORKFLOW-level: a change confined to those paths triggers no
lane at all. That was safe while the paths held inert prose, and is not: four of them are read
by tests, two of which byte-match a document against a code table. .github/workflows/docs.yml
triggers ON those paths and runs scripts/doc-gate.mjs.
registry-consistency.test.ts asserts that EVERY ci.yml paths-ignore glob is either covered by
docs.yml's trigger paths or listed in 'uncovered' below -- and, for each 'uncovered' glob, that
no test file actually reads that path. So the justification cannot silently go stale: the day a
test starts reading deploy/, the guard fails and the glob must move into docs.yml.

uncovered.deploy/**: Apache confs, the systemd unit and the deploy README. No test reads them; RUNBOOK.md covers the procedure. Move into docs.yml the moment one does.
